summary: Retest of the iteration_126 findings for the admin-panel performance work. 5 of the 6 retest points pass in the backend tests and the UI. One security gap is still open: PUT /api/admin/users/{id} still returns password_plain in its response. The frontend merges that response into the users list, so after an admin saves a legacy user the plaintext password shows up again as the 'Пароль: ...' preview. Reproduced in the UI on a throwaway TEST user. Backend: 22 of 23 tests pass (the new test_iter128_admin_retest.py plus the iter127 regression file). Frontend: race tests use page.route to delay stale requests by 3s. A stale search 'a' followed by a fast-typed '50d0deb5' showed only #50d0deb5. Clicking pending, then cancelled, then completed tabs, with the first two delayed, showed only completed orders (50 rows). The tab click and the manager-filter change both reset to page 1 at once, and only page=1 requests were sent. The header reads 'Всего 868 заказов (найдено: N)', and the stat cards stay global under filters while the pagination follows the filtered count. 'Откатить' shows only on completed and processing orders, not on cancelled or partially_fulfilled ones. The CRM edit modal password field is empty, also for a legacy user that still has password_plain in the DB. Saving without a password kept the original login working. The admin Overview still loads and shows 868 orders.

critical.issue: The response projection (admin.py line 278: {'_id':0,'password':0}) does not exclude password_plain, plain_password or password_hash. 20 users in the DB still have legacy password_plain, including the real client 0x0errorr@gmail.com. Any admin edit of such a user without a password change returns the plaintext in the response, and AdminPage.handleSaveUser merges res.data into the users list, so the plaintext reappears in the list as user-password-preview-{id}. Reproduced on a TEST user.

minor.issue: log_state (admin.py line 295) strips password, password_plain and password_hash but not plain_password, so legacy plain_password can be saved into the action log's before_state.

20 users still have a password_plain field. Consider a one-time $unset migration; the owner must approve it because it is real data. Note: auth.py line 165 still accepts password_plain as a change-password fallback.

Slow on Overview: dashboard took 2.3-7.0s and attention 3.3-5.1s. AdminPage also fires duplicate calls on one load (admin/dashboard x4, admin/attention x4, admin/orders x3, admin/users x3, admin/stats x3). Related to the 'admin panel slow' goal but not part of this retest scope.

ui_bugs.issue: Because the PUT response leaks password_plain and is merged into the users state, the 'Пароль: <plaintext>' preview (lines 1803-1806) shows again after saving a legacy user. The dead UI code that renders password_plain (lines 1803, 1881, 3338-3341) should also be removed.

action_items: backend/routes/admin.py update_admin_user: change the final find_one projection to {'_id':0,'password':0,'password_plain':0,'plain_password':0,'password_hash':0}.
Remove the password_plain rendering code from AdminPage.js (lines ~1803, ~1881, ~3338) so nothing can show plaintext even if the API regresses.
Add plain_password to the excluded keys in delete_admin_user log_state.
Optional, needs owner approval: a one-time $unset of password_plain/plain_password across users, and drop the plaintext fallback in auth.py change-password.
Optional performance: remove the duplicate admin API calls on AdminPage mount and look at /admin/dashboard (up to 7s).
critical_code_review_comments: AdminOrdersPage: the requestSeqRef guard and the setPage(1) batching are correct. The extra identical request seen in the network log is the 10s poll, not a double fire.
The iter127 test test_flat_array still asserts min(db_total, 1000). It passes now only because there are 868 orders; update it to 5000 to match the new cap.
models.py AdminUserResponse still declares password_plain. Remove it so it can't be serialized by accident.
AdminPage.js is 3817 lines and AdminOrdersPage.js 1055 lines; both should be split.
The merge button stays disabled when the 2 selected orders belong to different clients. This is intended ('Выберите минимум 2 заказа одного клиента').

success_rate.frontend: 92% (all retest points pass; the password preview shows again after saving a legacy user)

seed_data_creation: Created 2 throwaway TEST users (test_iter128_*@example.com from pytest and test_iter128ui@example.com from the UI test). Both were deleted by id through DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}. No real data was modified; the legacy user 0x0errorr@gmail.com edit modal was only opened and then cancelled.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_iter128_admin_retest.py tests/test_iter127_admin_perf_pagination.py --noconftest -p no:xdist. test_put_response_no_password_plain sets password_plain on its own TEST user to simulate a legacy account. The race was reproduced with page.route delaying status=pending|cancelled or search=a requests by 3s. Order ids for the rollback check: cancelled f15ee199, partially_fulfilled 19a40d62, completed 50d0deb5, processing 7e8e5b47. Destructive order actions (merge/fulfill/cancel/delete) were not re-run in the UI this round; their handlers only gained fetchOrders() refresh calls (git diff checked).
rca of the issue: The password fix covered GET /admin/users and GET /admin/users/{id}/details but missed the PUT /admin/users/{id} response (admin.py:278, which projects out only 'password'). The frontend handleSaveUser does setUsers(u => ({...u, ...res.data})), so the leaked field goes back into the list state and the existing password_plain preview code renders it. Reproduce: a user with password_plain in the DB → CRM → Edit → Save without a password → 'Пароль: <plain>' appears under the user. Fix: exclude the password fields in the PUT projection and delete the UI render paths.
